derivedLineProposals.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1): The round structure is draw 2 / discard 1, netting +1 card per round; starting at 3 cards and ending at 10 cards means 7 rounds, matching the 7 discards stated as the count at game end.
citedBothStatements: Each player draws 2 cards into their hand each round.
Each player discards 1 card per round.
Each player draws 3 cards from the mess to form their starting hand.
The game ends when all players have 10 cards.
Players will have 7 discards when the game ends.
derivedLineProposals.arithmeticNote: Net cards per round = draw 2 minus discard 1 = +1/round. Span = ending hand size (10) minus starting hand size (3) = 7. Rounds = span (7) divided by net-per-round (1) = 7 rounds, which the line then compares against the independently-stated 7-discards-at-game-end fact. Operands: 'Each player draws 2 cards into their hand each round.', 'Each player discards 1 card per round.', 'Each player draws 3 cards from the mess to form their starting hand.' (starting size 3), 'The game ends when all players have 10 cards.' (ending size 10), and 'Players will have 7 discards when the game ends.' (the value being matched against).

listA.statement: The Jab action card has a timing value of 1.
listA.sourceSentence: p.2, JAB (TIMING: 1), italic:

listA.statement: If both boxers are in their corners, a Jab does nothing.
listA.sourceSentence: If both boxers are in their corners: Do nothing. You can't reach your opponent!

listA.statement: If the boxers are not both in their corners, a Jab flips one of the opponent's Guard cards from ready to exhausted.
listA.sourceSentence: If not: Flip one of your opponent's Guard cards from ready to exhausted.

listA.statement: If all of the opponent's Guard cards are already exhausted, the Jab does nothing.
listA.sourceSentence: If all their Guard cards are already exhausted, do nothing.

listA.statement: A Jab can never break a Guard card.
listA.sourceSentence: A Jab cannot break a Guard card (see Punch).

listA.statement: The Retreat action card has a timing value of 2.
listA.sourceSentence: p.2, RETREAT (TIMING: 2), italic:

listA.statement: Retreat does nothing if the player is already in their corner.
listA.sourceSentence: If you are already in your corner: Do nothing. You're already against the ropes!

listA.statement: Retreat moves a boxer from the center ring to their own corner.
listA.sourceSentence: If you are in the center ring: Move your boxer to your corner.

listA.statement: The Advance action card has a timing value of 3.
listA.sourceSentence: p.2, ADVANCE (TIMING: 3), italic:

listA.statement: Advance does nothing if the player is already in the center ring, and it also does nothing if both players play an Advance card for the same action.
listA.sourceSentence: If you are already in the center ring and/or your opponent also plays an Advance card for the same action: Do nothing. You're just butting heads!

listA.statement: Otherwise, Advance moves the player's boxer into the center ring.
listA.sourceSentence: If not: Move your boxer to the center ring.

listA.statement: When a player Advances into the center ring and the opponent is there, the opponent is pushed into their own corner.
listA.sourceSentence: If your opponent is in the center ring, also push them into their corner.

listA.statement: Worked example: with Blue in their corner and Red in the center, Blue's Advance moves Blue to the center and pushes Red back to Red's corner.
listA.sourceSentence: For example, Blue is in their corner and Red is in the center ring. Blue moves into the center ring, and Red is pushed back into their own corner.

listA.statement: The Block action card has a timing value of 4.
listA.sourceSentence: p.2, BLOCK (TIMING: 4), italic:

listA.statement: If the opponent plays a Punch card for the same action, Block causes that Punch's effect on the blocking player to be ignored.
listA.sourceSentence: If your opponent plays a Punch card for the same action: Ignore any effect their Punch has on you (see Punch).

listA.statement: Block does not stop Jabs.
listA.sourceSentence: Block actions do not block Jabs.

listA.statement: If the opponent does not play a Punch for the same action, Block does nothing.
listA.sourceSentence: If not: Do nothing.

listA.statement: The Punch action card has a timing value of 5.
listA.sourceSentence: p.2, PUNCH (TIMING: 5), italic:

listA.statement: Punching from your own corner requires first flipping one of your own Guard cards from ready to exhausted, then resolving the Punch.
listA.sourceSentence: If you are in your corner: Flip one of your Guard cards from ready to exhausted, then resolve your Punch.

listA.statement: A player in their corner with no ready Guard cards does nothing when Punching.
listA.sourceSentence: If you do not have any ready Guard cards, do nothing. You're up against the ropes!

listA.statement: Punching from the center ring resolves without flipping any of your own Guard cards.
listA.sourceSentence: If you are in the center ring: Resolve your Punch without flipping your Guard card. You've got 'em on the ropes!

listA.statement: A blocked Punch, or a Punch thrown while both players are in their respective corners, has no effect on the opponent, but the punching player must still exhaust their own Guard card if they are in their corner.
listA.sourceSentence: If your Punch is blocked (see Block) or both you and your opponent are in your respective corners: Your Punch has no effect on your opponent; however, you must still exhaust your own guard card if you are in your corner.

listA.statement: An unblocked Punch against an opponent with at least one exhausted Guard card breaks one of those exhausted Guard cards, removing it from the game and returning it to the box.
listA.sourceSentence: If your Punch is not blocked and your opponent has at least one exhausted Guard card: Break one of your opponent's exhausted Guard cards by removing it from the game and returning it to the box.

listA.statement: An unblocked Punch against an opponent with no exhausted Guard cards flips one of their ready Guard cards to exhausted instead of breaking one.
listA.sourceSentence: If your Punch is not blocked and your opponent does not have any exhausted Guard cards: Instead of breaking their Guard, flip one of your opponent's Guard cards from ready to exhausted.

listA.statement: When both players Punch on the same action and one is in the center ring, the player punching from their corner must finish exhausting their Guard card (if able) before either Punch resolves.
listA.sourceSentence: If both you and your opponent play a Punch for the same action while one player is in the center ring: The player punching from their corner must finish exhausting their Guard card (if able) before either player may resolve their Punch.

listA.statement: Worked example: Blue in the corner and Red in the center both Punch; Blue exhausts a Guard first, then both Punches resolve.
listA.sourceSentence: For example, if Blue is in their corner and Red is in the center and they both Punch, Blue must first exhaust a Guard before both players Punch one another.

listA.statement: The Rest action card has a timing value of 6.
listA.sourceSentence: p.2, REST (TIMING: 6), italic:

listA.statement: Rest returns all action cards from your discard pile to your hand.
listA.sourceSentence: Reclaim your discards: Take all the action cards in your discard pile and add them to your hand.

listA.statement: Action cards currently in play are not picked up when Resting.
listA.sourceSentence: Do not take any of the action cards currently in play.

listA.statement: If any of your Guard cards are exhausted, Rest also flips one Guard card back to ready, in addition to reclaiming discards.
listA.sourceSentence: If any of your Guard cards are EXHAUSTED: Flip one Guard card back to ready. This is in addition to reclaiming your discards.

listA.statement: After the first action cards are compared and resolved, they are left in place and not discarded; the second action cards are then flipped face up and compared and resolved the same way.
listA.sourceSentence: When you are done comparing and resolving the first action cards, DO NOT discard them yet. Leave them in place and flip the second action cards face up. Then, compare and resolve the second action cards just like you did with the first action cards.

listA.statement: Example: a player punched while holding one ready and two exhausted Guards loses one exhausted Guard.
listA.sourceSentence: If you are punched and have one ready and two exhausted Guards, you would lose one exhausted Guard.

listA.statement: Example: a player punched while holding three ready and no exhausted Guards simply exhausts one card, ending with one exhausted and two ready.
listA.sourceSentence: If instead, you have three ready and no exhausted Guards, you would simply exhaust one card, leaving you with one exhausted and two ready.

listA.statement: The Discard phase is the third phase of a round.
listA.sourceSentence: p.2, 3) DISCARD:

listA.statement: After both sets of action cards are compared and resolved, each player places the two action cards they played that round into their discard pile and a new round begins.
listA.sourceSentence: After you have compared and resolved both the first and second sets of action cards, place your two action cards played this round into your discard pile, and then begin a new round.

listA.statement: No cards may be discarded before the Discard phase.
listA.sourceSentence: DO NOT DISCARD ANY CARDS UNTIL THIS PHASE.

listA.statement: A player who has broken all 3 of their opponent's Guard cards has knocked them out and immediately wins the game.
listA.sourceSentence: Once a player has broken all 3 of their opponent's Guard cards, they have knocked them out and immediately win the game!

listA.statement: If both players knock each other out during the same action, the game is a draw.
listA.sourceSentence: If both players manage to knock each other out during the same action, it is a draw.

listA.statement: A player should never hold both Rest cards in hand at the same time; if that happens, they likely picked up their current action cards while Resting.
listA.sourceSentence: You should never have both rest cards in your hand at the same time. If you do, you likely accidentally picked up your current action cards while Resting.

listA.statement: When Resting, pick up only the cards in the discard pile and not the two action cards from that round.
listA.sourceSentence: When Resting, only pick up the cards currently in your discard pile and not the two action cards from that round.

listA.statement: A player in their corner may still choose to play a Punch card with no ready Guard card; the Punch simply has no effect and does not force them to break their own Guard card.
listA.sourceSentence: If you are in your corner, you need a ready Guard card for a Punch to work; however, you may still choose to play a Punch card but it won't have any effect. This would not force you to break your own Guard card.

listA.statement: The game state can change mid-round — for example, an opponent's Jab exhausting your last ready Guard leaves you with no Guard to exhaust for your own Punch from the corner.
listA.sourceSentence: The state of the game may change in the middle of a round. For example, if your opponent Jabs and exhausts your last ready Guard just as you are attempting to Punch from your corner, you will no longer have a Guard card to exhaust.

listA.statement: During the plan phase, action cards may be placed in any order regardless of their timing values; timing does not matter in that phase.
listA.sourceSentence: In the plan phase, you may place any action cards, regardless of their timings, in any order. The timing on the cards does not matter in this phase.

listA.statement: Example of free plan-phase ordering: a Rest (timing 6) may be the first action and a Jab (timing 1) the second.
listA.sourceSentence: For example, you can play a Rest (timing 6) as your first action and a Jab (timing 1) as your second action.

listA.statement: In the fight phase, the first set of action cards is always fully resolved before the second set.
listA.sourceSentence: In the fight phase, the first set of action cards are always completely resolved before the second set of action cards.

listA.statement: Example of strict set ordering: a Block played as the first action does not stop a Punch played as the second action.
listA.sourceSentence: For example, a Block from the first action will not stop a Punch from the second action.

derivedLineProposals.derivedLineText: Derived (p.2): A "broken" Guard card is permanently removed from the game (returned to the box), distinct from "exhausted" (flipped face, remains in play and can be flipped back to ready by Rest). Punch can only break an already-exhausted Guard card; against an opponent with no exhausted Guards, Punch instead exhausts one of their ready Guards (same effect as a Jab in that case).
citedBothStatements: An unblocked Punch against an opponent with at least one exhausted Guard card breaks one of those exhausted Guard cards.
An unblocked Punch against an opponent with no exhausted Guard cards flips one of their ready Guard cards to exhausted instead of breaking.
If any Guard cards are exhausted, Rest also flips one Guard card back to ready, in addition to reclaiming discards.

derivedLineProposals.derivedLineText: Derived (p.2): Resolving a round's Fight phase is two sequential sub-steps — resolve both players' first action cards completely (in timing order), then reveal and resolve both players' second action cards (in timing order) — with cards from the first sub-step staying in place, unresolved into the discard pile, until the Discard phase.
citedBothStatements: In the fight phase, the first set of action cards is always fully resolved before the second set.
First action cards are left in place (not discarded) and the second action cards are flipped face up, then compared and resolved the same way as the first.
No cards may be discarded before the Discard phase.

derivedLineProposals.derivedLineText: Derived (p.2): Win condition: reduce an opponent to 0 Guard cards (all 3 broken) to knock them out and win immediately. If both players' third Guard card is broken by the same action's resolution, the game ends in a draw instead of a win.
citedBothStatements: A player who breaks all 3 of opponent's Guard cards knocks them out and immediately wins the game.
If both players knock each other out during the same action, the game is a draw.

listA.statement: The game proceeds in a repeating loop of two phases: Phase I (dice roll/resolution) and Phase II (the machine phase).
listA.sourceSentence: PHASE I: DICE ROLL / RESOLUTION - On each turn, you will roll your available dice, and allocate them in various ways to modify your rolls, defend against incoming damage, and deal damage to parts of the Doom Machine.

listA.statement: On each turn during Phase I, the player rolls their available dice.
listA.sourceSentence: PHASE I: DICE ROLL / RESOLUTION - On each turn, you will roll your available dice, and allocate them in various ways to modify your rolls, defend against incoming damage, and deal damage to parts of the Doom Machine.

listA.statement: Rolled dice are allocated to modify rolls, to defend against incoming damage, and to deal damage to parts of the Doom Machine.
listA.sourceSentence: PHASE I: DICE ROLL / RESOLUTION - On each turn, you will roll your available dice, and allocate them in various ways to modify your rolls, defend against incoming damage, and deal damage to parts of the Doom Machine.

listA.statement: Phase II begins only after the player has allocated and resolved all of their dice.
listA.sourceSentence: PHASE II: THE MACHINE PHASE - Once you have allocated and resolved all of your dice, the machine will cycle its remaining parts, resolve their effects, then grow by 1 additional card.

listA.statement: During the machine phase, the machine cycles its remaining parts and resolves their effects.
listA.sourceSentence: PHASE II: THE MACHINE PHASE - Once you have allocated and resolved all of your dice, the machine will cycle its remaining parts, resolve their effects, then grow by 1 additional card.

listA.statement: After cycling and resolving its parts, the machine grows by one additional card.
listA.sourceSentence: PHASE II: THE MACHINE PHASE - Once you have allocated and resolved all of your dice, the machine will cycle its remaining parts, resolve their effects, then grow by 1 additional card.

listA.statement: The phase loop repeats until one of two end conditions occurs: the player reveals and destroys the Doom Core, or the machine destroys the player.
listA.sourceSentence: This loop continues until either you have revealed and destroyed the Doom Core or you are destroyed by the machine.

listA.statement: The player wins by revealing and then destroying the Doom Core.
listA.sourceSentence: This loop continues until either you have revealed and destroyed the Doom Core or you are destroyed by the machine.

listA.statement: The player loses if they are destroyed by the machine.

listA.statement: The machine phase begins by processing machine part cards in play from left to right, cycling each card's track and resolving its abilities.
listA.sourceSentence: At the start of the machine phase, go from left to right down the row of machine parts in play, cycling each card's track and resolving its abilities as follows:

listA.statement: Cycling a machine part card means moving its yellow die one space down that card's cycle track.
listA.sourceSentence: 1) Move a machine part card's yellow die 1 space down its cycle track.

listA.statement: If the die lands on an icon after being moved, that icon's corresponding ability triggers immediately.
listA.sourceSentence: If that dice lands on an icon, immediately trigger that icon's corresponding ability.

listA.statement: In the example, Soul Harvester's HP die cycles one space down its track and triggers its damage icon ability.
listA.sourceSentence: The HP die for Soul Harvester will cycle one space down the track, triggering its [damage icon] ability, which will deal 5 damage to the player.

listA.statement: The triggered damage ability in the example deals 5 damage to the player.
listA.sourceSentence: The HP die for Soul Harvester will cycle one space down the track, triggering its [damage icon] ability, which will deal 5 damage to the player.

listA.statement: A player's shields can prevent some or all of incoming damage.
listA.sourceSentence: If they don't have enough shields to prevent some or all of that damage.

listA.statement: Damage that is not blocked carries over and reduces the player's HP directly.
listA.sourceSentence: Unblocked damage carries over and reduces HP directly.

listA.statement: If moving a die places it on a dead space (a darkened square), the die is instead moved back to the track's starting position.
listA.sourceSentence: Note: If moving the die places it on a dead space (darkened square), then move that die back to the starting position on the track.

listA.statement: After cycling one card, play proceeds rightward to the next machine part card and repeats the cycling process.
listA.sourceSentence: 2) Proceed to the next machine part card in the line (moving right) and repeat the card cycling process until all part cards have increased their cycle track by 1 and resolved any abilities/effects that are triggered.

listA.statement: The cycling repetition continues until every machine part card has advanced its cycle track by one and resolved any triggered abilities or effects.
listA.sourceSentence: 2) Proceed to the next machine part card in the line (moving right) and repeat the card cycling process until all part cards have increased their cycle track by 1 and resolved any abilities/effects that are triggered.

listA.statement: After all cards have cycled, the entire machine part card row is slid one space to the right.
listA.sourceSentence: 3) Now, carefully slide the entire machine part card row one space to the right.

listA.statement: A new machine part card is drawn and placed into the space made available by sliding the row.
listA.sourceSentence: Draw a new machine part card and slot it into the available space.

listA.statement: A yellow HP die is placed on the first cycle tracking space of the newly added card.

listA.statement: The machine cycle is complete once all machine part cards have cycled and a new card has been added to the line.
listA.sourceSentence: When all machine part cards have cycled and a new card is added to the line, gather all of your spent dice (including any new dice you may have obtained by defeating machine parts) and return to Phase I.

listA.statement: When a machine part card deals damage to you, that damage is applied to your shields before anything else, provided you still have shields remaining.

listA.statement: Taking damage reduces the value of your shield dice first.

listA.statement: A shield die that is completely expended is removed to your spent dice pile.
listA.sourceSentence: As damage is taken, reduce the value of shield dice first until they are completely expended (and removed to your spent dice pile).

listA.statement: Damage not absorbed by shield dice carries over and is applied directly to your HP.

listA.statement: Destroying the Doom Core wins the game.
listA.sourceSentence: You win the game when the Doom Core has been destroyed.

listA.statement: Winning does not require clearing all machine part cards.
listA.sourceSentence: You don't have to clear all of the machine part cards to win.

listA.statement: If your HP reaches zero, you lose the game because the machine destroys you first.
listA.sourceSentence: However, if your HP is reduced to zero, the machine destroys you first, and you lose.

listA.statement: The card art source PDF has four letter-sized pages laid out as a 3x3 grid of cards per page.
listA.sourceSentence: Source: `/Users/jtsmith/BoardSmithGames/doom-machine/cards.pdf` (4 letter pages, 3x3 grid per page).

listA.statement: Pages 1 and 3 of the PDF contain card faces, totalling 18 faces.
listA.sourceSentence: **p.1 and p.3 = card FACES** (18 faces total).

listA.statement: Pages 2 and 4 contain card backs, all showing the "DOOM MACHINE / BY NATHAN MEUNIER" back art except one slot.
listA.sourceSentence: **p.2 and p.4 = card BACKS** — confirmed: every slot is the "DOOM MACHINE / BY NATHAN MEUNIER" back art, EXCEPT p.2 row 1 col 3, which is the **Player HP card's B side**

listA.statement: The Player HP card's B side sits at p.2 row 1 col 3 and is the duplex mirror of the Player HP A side at p.1 row 1 col 1.
listA.sourceSentence: EXCEPT p.2 row 1 col 3, which is the **Player HP card's B side** (the duplex-mirror of the Player HP A side at p.1 row 1 col 1).

listA.statement: Page 4 consists of nine identical card backs with no exceptions.
listA.sourceSentence: p.4 is nine identical backs, no exceptions.

listA.statement: The game includes 15 machine part cards that are not the Core.
listA.sourceSentence: - 15 machine part cards (non-Core)

listA.statement: The game includes one Doom Core card, named "THE DOOM CORE".
listA.sourceSentence: - 1 Doom Core card ("THE DOOM CORE")

listA.statement: The game includes one Doom Machine tracking card.
listA.sourceSentence: - 1 Doom Machine tracking card

listA.statement: The game includes one double-sided Player HP tracking card, with the A side on p.1 and the B side on p.2.
listA.sourceSentence: - 1 Player HP tracking card (double-sided: A side p.1, B side p.2)

listA.statement: There are 18 distinct card faces in total.
listA.sourceSentence: - **18 distinct faces total.**

listA.statement: A card's cycle track is L-shaped: three squares run down the left edge, then two more run right along the bottom.
listA.sourceSentence: three squares running DOWN the left edge, then two more running RIGHT along the bottom.

listA.statement: Cycle-track positions 2 through 5 contain icons, blanks, or dead spaces, and the die travels in the order 1 to 2 to 3 to 4 to 5.
listA.sourceSentence: Positions 2–5 hold icons, blanks, or dead spaces. Order of travel = 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5.

listA.statement: Three kinds of cycle-track space exist.
listA.sourceSentence: Three kinds of space appear:

listA.statement: An icon space is a live space carrying an effect badge, joined to its neighbours by a yellow connector bar.
listA.sourceSentence: - **Icon space** — a live space with an effect badge. Connected to its neighbours by a YELLOW connector bar.

listA.statement: A blank space is a live, plain dark-teal space with no icon, so no effect fires; it is also yellow-connected.
listA.sourceSentence: - **Blank space** — a live space, plain dark-teal, no icon (no effect fires). Also YELLOW-connected.

listA.statement: A dead space is a darkened, diagonally hatched square connected by dull grey/teal bars rather than yellow ones.
listA.sourceSentence: - **Dead space** — a DARKENED, diagonally-HATCHED square. Connected by dull grey/teal bars, not yellow.

listA.statement: Landing on a dead space sends the die back to position 1 of the cycle track.
listA.sourceSentence: Per the rulebook (`02-machine-phase.md`), landing on a dead space sends the die back to position 1.

listA.statement: The Player HP A side is the normal-mode side of the Player HP tracking card.
listA.sourceSentence: - **Type:** Player HP tracking card (A side / normal mode)

listA.statement: The Player HP card has no starting HP of its own; it is a tracker and the rules set its cube to 10.
listA.sourceSentence: - **Starting HP:** n/a (this is the tracker; rules set the cube to 10)

listA.statement: The Player HP A side is printed with the words PLAYER HP, A SIDE, SHIELD, 1X ROUND, and UTILITY.
listA.sourceSentence: - QUOTE — cards.pdf p.1, row 1 col 1: "PLAYER HP"

listA.statement: The A side of the Player HP card is explicitly labelled "A SIDE".
listA.sourceSentence: - QUOTE — cards.pdf p.1, row 1 col 1: "A SIDE"

listA.statement: The Player HP A side has a heart badge above a serpentine numbered track reading 10, 9 / 7, 8 / 6, 5 / 3, 4 / 2, 1 / 0.
listA.sourceSentence: - **PLAYER HP track:** heart badge at top, then a serpentine numbered track: 10, 9 / 7, 8 / 6, 5 / 3, 4 / 2, 1 / 0.

listA.statement: The Player HP track has 11 spaces running from 10 down to 0.
listA.sourceSentence: (11 spaces, 10 down to 0.)

listA.statement: The Player HP A side's shield section has four slots, shown as shield-with-plus badges in a 2x2 arrangement.
listA.sourceSentence: - **SHIELD section: 4 slots.** Four shield-with-"+" badges in a 2x2 arrangement.

listA.statement: The Player HP A side's utility section, labelled "1X ROUND", has six slots in total.
listA.sourceSentence: - **UTILITY section (labelled "1X ROUND"): 6 slots total —**

listA.statement: Three of the A side's utility slots are "+/-" roll-modifier slots.
listA.sourceSentence: - **3 x "+/-" roll-modifier slots**

listA.statement: Three of the A side's utility slots are re-roll slots marked with a two-white-dice glyph.
listA.sourceSentence: - **3 x re-roll slots** (two-white-dice glyph)

listA.statement: The A side utility slots are laid out as row 1 two roll-modifiers, row 2 one roll-modifier and one re-roll, row 3 two re-rolls.
listA.sourceSentence: - Printed layout: row 1 = [+/-] [+/-]; row 2 = [+/-] [dice]; row 3 = [dice] [dice].

listA.statement: The Player HP A side has no roll conditions, no cycle track, and no destroy effect.
listA.sourceSentence: - No roll conditions, no cycle track, no destroy effect.

listA.statement: The Doom Machine card is a tracking card with no starting HP.
listA.sourceSentence: - **Type:** Doom Machine tracking card

listA.statement: The Doom Machine tracking card's entire printed text is THE, DOOM, MACHINE, SENTIENCE, POWER plus the two track numeral sequences.
listA.sourceSentence: - **COMPLETE VERBATIM TRANSCRIPTION — every word printed on this card:**

listA.statement: The Doom Machine card's Sentience track numerals read, top to bottom, 10 9 7 8 6 5 3 4 2 1 0.
listA.sourceSentence: - QUOTE (Sentience track numerals, top to bottom): "10" "9" "7" "8" "6" "5" "3" "4" "2" "1" "0"

listA.statement: The Doom Machine card's Power track numerals read, top to bottom, 10 9 7 8 6 5 3 4 2 1 0.
listA.sourceSentence: - QUOTE (Power track numerals, top to bottom): "10" "9" "7" "8" "6" "5" "3" "4" "2" "1" "0"

listA.statement: Nothing else is printed on the Doom Machine tracking card beyond the transcribed text.
listA.sourceSentence: - **That is the entire printed content of the card. There is no other text of any kind.**

listA.statement: The Doom Machine card shows a yellow eye badge for Sentience above the left track, a black battery badge for Power above the right track, the logo plate between them, and two parallel serpentine 0–10 tracks.
listA.sourceSentence:
- Art: an eye badge (Sentience, yellow) above the left track, a battery badge (Power, black) above the right track,
the "THE DOOM MACHINE" logo plate between them. Two parallel serpentine 0–10 tracks.

listA.statement: The Doom Machine tracking card does not define what the Power and Sentience tracks do; it defines only their range of 0 through 10, with no threshold, trigger, win/loss condition, or per-turn effect printed.
listA.sourceSentence:
It defines only their RANGE (0 through 10). No threshold, no trigger, no win/loss condition, no per-turn effect
is printed anywhere on it.

listA.statement: Extinction Collider at p.3 r1c1 reads damage equal to Power.
listA.sourceSentence: - EXTINCTION COLLIDER (p.3 r1c1): "DEAL DMG = POWER"

listA.statement: Synaptic Disruptor at p.3 r3c2 reads damage equal to Sentience.
listA.sourceSentence: - SYNAPTIC DISRUPTOR (p.3 r3c2): "DEAL DMG = SENTIENCE"

listA.statement: The Doom Core at p.3 r1c3 reads damage equal to Sentience plus Power.
listA.sourceSentence: - THE DOOM CORE (p.3 r1c3): "DEAL DMG = SENTIENCE + POWER"

listA.statement: Cerebral Amplifier at p.1 r3c1 deals 3 more damage if Sentience is greater than 5.
listA.sourceSentence: - CEREBRAL AMPLIFIER (p.1 r3c1): "IF SENTIENCE IS > 5 DEAL 3 MORE DMG"

listA.statement: Stasis Generator at p.3 r2c2 removes the die from play if Sentience is greater than 6.
listA.sourceSentence: - STASIS GENERATOR (p.3 r2c2): "IF SENTIENCE IS > 6 REMOVE THAT DIE FROM PLAY"

listA.statement: Power and Sentience act as damage/severity multipliers consumed by specific cards, and no printed rule exists for reaching the top of a track or for a track-based loss condition.
listA.sourceSentence:
So Power and Sentience are damage/severity multipliers consumed by specific cards. There is still NO printed
rule for what happens at the top of a track (10), and no track-based loss condition anywhere in the PDFs.
